usual_baseline: Enhanced recovery is patchy. Only 36% of Scottish units had a programme and 35% of patients were catheterised. Day 0 or 24-hour mobilisation runs about 66%. Length of stay was 3.6 days in one unit; same-day hip discharge was 54.3% in another.
fix_that_works: A multidisciplinary group with parallel PDSA cycles (local infiltration, preprinted charts, nurse-led mobilisation, ring-fenced ward) cut stay from 3.6 to 2.4 days for hips and 2.0 for knees [1591]. Feedback to the team: 24-hour mobilisation 66.0% to 90.5% [1730]. Spinal lidocaine: same-day discharge 54.3% to 80.6% [1734]. National steering: programmes 36% to 68%, catheterisation 35% to 26% [1475].
fix_that_fails: No failed fix reported in these audits. Median stay did not change (2 days) despite better mobilisation [1730]. Physiotherapy stayed rare on day 0: none documented in one unit [1730] and 3.5% of first mobilisations in another [1591].
consultant_advice: Measuring length of stay alone tells you little. Audit single elements that decide discharge: day 0 mobilisation, pain and nausea control, catheter use. Pain was the commonest barrier to discharge [1730]. Record 30-day readmissions and complications alongside, as same-day discharge audits did [1734].
